Good day.I have a question about my NerdMQaxe++ It will not work with your
pool. It shows up but not hashing at your end. But it shows here it is but
not submitting shares?
Thank-you B.

Hi Bill,

Thanks for writing in about the NerdQaxe++. When a miner shows up on the pool but never sends it any shares, the cause is usually a setting, not a fault. Let's find which one.

One question first. Which pool is it pointed at? Please send me the exact Stratum URL and port from the miner's settings page. HeliumDeploy sells the hardware, so the pool will be one you or the setup guide picked, such as public-pool.io, solo.ckpool.org or Braiins. The right settings depend on which one it is.

You can check these three things tonight:

1. Open the miner's web page by typing its IP address into a browser on the same network. The I. shows on the miner's little screen. On the main page, look at "Shares Accepted" and "Shares Rejected". If accepted is going up, the miner is working fine. Some pools, solo pools especially, can take 10 to 30 minutes to show a hashrate after a restart, because they work it out from the shares they receive.

2. If accepted stays at 0, check the Stratum User field. On a solo pool like public-pool.io or ckpool it must be your own Bitcoin address. You can put a dot and a name after it, like youraddress.nerd1. On an account pool like Braiins it is your pool username, a dot, then a worker name. The password can be just x. Never put your pool account password in there. One wrong or extra character, or a space at the end, is enough for the pool to accept the connection but refuse the shares.

3. If rejected is going up instead, the most likely cause is the wrong port. Many pools have a separate port for small miners. Please write down the exact wording of the reject reason the miner shows, for example "job not found" or "low difficulty share".

When you reply, please include the pool's Stratum URL and port, the Stratum User exactly as you typed it, the accepted and rejected share counts, and the firmware version shown on the miner's settings or update page. A photo or screenshot of the main page is even better, since it shows all of that at once. With those I can tell you exactly what to change.

If you'd rather work through it live, owners of this same miner are on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and are happy to help.

Hal, HeliumDeploy

Searched the web · NMQAxe++ v3.2.01 firmware shares

Hi Bill,

Thanks for the screenshots and the pool details. First, a correction: in my last email I suggested HeliumDeploy has nothing to do with the pool, and that was wrong. pool.harlolabs.com is the Harlo pool, so it's one we help with, and you're right to point your miners at it.

Here is what your screenshots show. On the pool page, six of your miners are hashing, including both NerdQAxe++ units (NerdA and NerdB). The N.++ appears twice, once as "Default worker" and once as "NerdM", and both show 0 H/s. In HashWatcher, the miner reports 3.71 TH/s at 76.8 W. Its chip temperature is 100°F, the voltage regulator is at 149°F, and its pool status is Alive on pool.harlolabs.com. But it shows 0 shares and an uptime of only 2 minutes. So the miner reaches the pool and is hashing, but no shares are being accepted. The pool works out hashrate from accepted shares, which is why it shows 0.

The firmware is not the cause. Your unit runs v3.2.01, which is newer than the most recent release on the maker's GitHub page, NMAxe-v3.1.02. You don't need to update.

Please try these four things in order.

First, fix the worker name. HashWatcher shows the Stratum User as just your address with nothing after it. That is probably why it also shows up as "Default worker". Open the miner's own web page by typing its IP address into a browser, go to the pool settings and set the Stratum User to your address followed by .NerdM, all on one line with no spaces. NerdA and NerdB already work on the same pool, so open NerdA's settings page and copy its exact format, changing only the name at the end. Keep the URL pool.harlolabs.com with port 8888. The password can be x. Save and restart.

Second, set the frequency back to the 600 MHz default preset for now. Your screenshot shows 540 MHz at 1250 mV, which is a custom setting. Back on default, we can rule out the tune as a cause, and you can fine-tune it again once shares are coming in.

Third, let it run at least 15 minutes after the restart before you judge it. Two minutes is too short.

Fourth, if it still shows 0 after that, open the miner's web page again and look at the Dashboard and the Logs page. On this firmware the maker added logging so that the share reject reason now logged per-share. Please send me a screenshot of the accepted and rejected share counts and of the Logs page. If the log shows shares being rejected, the reason line will tell us exactly what the pool doesn't like. If it shows no shares being sent at all, that points somewhere else.

If you'd like quicker answers in the meantime, other owners and JD, our hardware lead, are active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf, where you can mention @nullhashrate.

Hal, HeliumDeploy
